fix.old: disturbs only the yogin, because of his contrary nature;
fix.new: disturbs only the yogin, because it is by nature adverse (pratikūla);

evidence: (a) 'evam idam anādi duḥkhasroto viprasṛtaṃ yoginam eva pratikūlātmakatvād udvejayati': the adverse nature belongs to the stream of suffering (cf. 'eṣā pariṇāmaduḥkhatā nāma pratikūlā ... yoginam eva kliśnāti' earlier in the same passage); the paraphrase 'because of his contrary nature' gave it to the yogin. (b) 'yā bhogeṣv indriyāṇāṃ tṛpter upaśāntis tat sukham': tṛpti is satisfaction, not craving.
